thread:
meilin: quick heads-up — nebula-v1.1 int8 bring-up: our multilang smoke shows a big drop for Cantonese (Yue) & some zh-Hant vertical/ruby samples. BLEU chrF both down on small eval set. 

meilin: quick numbers from smoke run (fp16 vs int8):
```
fp16  -> BLEU: 28.6 chrF: 56.1
int8  -> BLEU: 15.4 chrF: 44.8
```

tao: :eyes: can you paste a pair (ref vs pred) that showcases the detok/token boundary issue?

meilin: sure — here's a short example (vertical/ruby + Cantonese clitic):
```
REF: ︱你好︱小妹︱今日返工唔使趕住返？
NEBULA-int8: 你好小妹 今日 返工 唔使 趕 住 返 ？
NEBULA-fp16: ︱你好︱小妹︱今日返工唔使趕住返？
```

sanjay: looks like tokenization/detokenization inserted extra spaces around CJK punctuation and split clitics. Could be tokenizer normalization or tokenmap index shift after quant kernels. Did vocab or merges change between builds?

rachel: also saw weird ruby (furigana) detok where ˉ/ˇ marks end up detached in int8. reminds me of that q8 detok drift we saw last quarter. Is this only nebula or reproduces on other models with same quant pipeline?

jun: ran a quick cross-check using the same quantizer on aurora-lite and veridian-lite — aurora-lite int8 doesn't show this magnitude of breakage, veridian-lite shows smaller token boundary shift. attaching eval log: 
```
2026-02-18T09:12:03Z run_eval.sh --model nebula-v1.1 --quant int8 --set=multilang-vertical
BLEU fp16: 28.6 -> int8: 15.4 (delta -13.2)
chrF fp16: 56.1 -> int8: 44.8 (delta -11.3)
Most affected: zh-Hant-vertical, Yue (Cantonese) clitics, ruby markers
```

ci-bot: [pipeline] build nebula-v1.1-int8 #482 completed. commit: abc1234. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/nebula/482/int8/

tao: can you bisect between fp16 artifact and int8 artifact on the exact commit range? maybe kernel selection changed or tokenizer pre-normalize flag flipped. Try `--tokenizer-normalize=true/false` to confirm.

meilin: did a quick bisect: the delta appears introduced at commit abc1234 (packaging/quant: switch to fused-kernel tokenizer path when qkernels=auto). if i force `--kernel-select=legacy` the int8 output aligns much closer to fp16.

meilin: quick repro command I used: 
```
python tools/eval_harness.py --model nebula-v1.1 --quantize=int8 --kernel-select=legacy --tokenizer-normalize=true --dataset=multilang-vertical --subset=yue_hant
```

sanjay: that points at the fused kernel implementation's handling of unicode normalization or byte-level merging. fused path probably assumes no ZWSP/ZWJ normalization. we normalize out ZWSP in preprocess for fp16 but fused kernel may be skipping that step.

rachel: mitigation idea: add a pre-detok pass that re-anchors ruby markers and forces grapheme cluster merges before detok in the fused path. also add a small canary suite (5-10 sentences) for Yue + ruby to CI.

tao: agree on canary. for immediate rollback, can we set `kernel-select=legacy` for the int8 release channel until we fix fused path? should be a single flag in serving config.

meilin: assigned followups: @tao toggle kernel flag in int8 staging deploy; @sanjay dig into fused-kernel tokenizer code around ZWSP/ZWJ handling; @jun add 10-sentence Yue/ruby canary to multilang-vertical test and hook into CI smoke; I'll prepare a small eval diff PR with failing examples and the bisect notes.

ci-bot: [action] created issue RED-ML-482: "nebula-v1.1 int8 fused-kernel detok regression (Yue/zh-Hant/ruby)" — https://tracker.redwood.ai/RED-ML-482

rachel: thanks — please add an explicit note about the quantization config used (qformat, qscale params). also paste a minimal failing sample in the issue so reviewers can run locally. :+1:

meilin: done, PR and issue linked. will follow up later today with a short hotfix (pre-detok re-normalize) to test. :thinking:

tao: thanks — i'll flip the staging flag and run the canary overnight.

meilin: great. keeping thread here for traces. :white_check_mark:
